title: Full-boundary Kummer algebra of a tame monomial trait chart
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $A=\mathbf F_\ell$, and let $R$ be a Noetherian local domain of dimension one with principal maximal ideal $(\pi)$, with $\ell$ invertible in $R$. For $d\geq1$, $s\geq0$, and positive integers $a_1,\ldots,a_d$ all invertible in $R$, put
$$P=R[z_1,\ldots,z_d,w_1,\ldots,w_s]/(z_1^{a_1}\cdots z_d^{a_d}-\pi).$$
Polynomial rings and spectra are [def-weil-polynomial-ring, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $\bar y$ be a geometric point of $\operatorname{Spec}P$ above $(\pi)$ [def-weil-geometric-point], let $H=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{\operatorname{Spec}P,\bar y}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], and let $I=\{j:z_j\text{ maps into the maximal ideal of }H\}$. Write $z_j$ also for its image in $H$, and put $W=\operatorname{Spec}H[1/\pi]$. On $W$ every $z_j$ is a unit. Use ordinary small-etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], Tate twists [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist], the Kummer connecting class $\kappa(z_j)\in H^1(W,A(1))$ [lem-amb-kummer-any-base], and its ordinary cup products [def-wf-ordinary-etale-cup]. For every $q\geq0$ the cup-product map
$$\bigwedge_A^q A^I\longrightarrow H^q(W,A(q)),\qquad e_{j_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge e_{j_q}\longmapsto\kappa(z_{j_1})\cup\cdots\cup\kappa(z_{j_q})$$
is an isomorphism; in degree zero it is the constant-section map. These maps together identify the exterior algebra with the diagonally twisted cohomology algebra. No excellence, completeness or henselianity of $R$ is assumed. Use the exterior algebra [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra]. Here $A^I$ is the free $A$-module with basis $e_j$ for $j\in I$, and $\bigwedge^q$ is the usual quotient of the $q$th tensor power imposing multilinearity and vanishing whenever two arguments coincide. In particular this assertion concerns the full generic open, where all boundary coordinates have been inverted.

source.place: Expose XVI Proposition 3.5.12, printed p.251, reference to the independent semistable calculation of Illusie (2004), On semistable reduction and the calculation of nearby cycles, Theorem 1.4, and Rapoport--Zink (1982), Satz 2.21. Agent-formulated full-boundary tame nearby-cycle input with invertible monomial multiplicities; the original references and this precise version are WANTED, not read.
